lines: The Everyone thread is the heart of a Popkin.
At the top: the Popkin's emoji and name, fourteen members, five here now.
Below, messages run oldest first, by day, with a note when someone pops in.
Someone else's message carries their avatar and first name.
Yours sits on the right, in the Popkin's colour, with its time.
Type a message and press Enter.
It appears in the thread at once, and the field empties.
Shift and Enter adds a line.
A message holds up to two thousand characters, and a count shows.
Chat is live. When Walt sends a message, you see it within a second, without reloading.
Assistive technology announces it politely, with its sender.
Reading older messages when one arrives? The view does not move.
New messages takes you to the latest.
A message is never lost silently.
If a send fails, it stays in the thread, marked Not sent, with Try again and Delete.
Try again, and it is sent.
Go offline, and a banner says so.
What you send is kept on the device, marked Waiting to send.
When the connection returns, it is sent in order: back online, two messages sent.

lines.text: On a phone the thread stands alone, with no tabs.
On a laptop, the sidebar and the list of conversations sit beside it.
Wider still, a third pane names who is here now.

lines: The list shows the latest message.
And every screen works in light and in dark.
What no screen shows, the tests prove.
A message tried again is stored once, and only a member reads the thread.
That is journey three. Popkin is a free platform for pop-up communities.
